Hi David,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our legal team reviewed the latest DPA draft and have two standing asks on retention/erasure language before we can route for exec sign-off:

1) A 90-day grace window for backup snapshots and disaster recovery copies before final irrecoverable deletion. We understand primary storage can be erased sooner, but backups are operationally different for us.
2) A carveout for lawful investigation/legal hold triggers where we may need a longer short-term hold (we suggested 90 days as well) while we coordinate with regulators or investigators.

We attached our redline (FinTech_DPA_v2_redline.docx) with inline comments and highlighted where the retention language should live. The SOC 2 re-assessment is scheduled for Oct so we need the DPA finalized within the next 4 weeks.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept the 90-day backup grace period or propose an alternative that preserves operational integrity? Also please indicate what proof or certification you can provide once backups are purged.

Appreciate a short reply with options, and happy to hop on a 30-min call if that speeds things up.

Best,

Gina — thanks for the clear asks and the redline. I've looped in Karthik and Laura from legal/ops. Quick summary of our thinking and a proposed middle ground:

- Backup grace window: operationally, holding immutable backups for 90 days increases storage and restore-scope complexity. We can offer a 60-day grace window for disaster recovery copies (snapshot TTL = 60 days) if we add two safeguards:
  * Snapshots are tombstoned on day 0 (marked for deletion) so they are not used for analytics or model training.
  * We provide a monthly proof-of-deletion report for snapshots (hash-based manifest) within 7 days after the TTL expires.

- Lawful/investigation holds: we understand the need for short-term holds. Proposal: Redwood will support customer-initiated holds up to 90 days with explicit request/attestation and an audit trail. Holds beyond 90 days require a formal legal process and review.

I'm attaching a draft schedule that maps TTLs and proof cadence (DPA_Schedule_v3.pdf). If that direction looks acceptable to FinTechCorp we can prepare a DPA paragraph that reflects these points and drop it into the redline.

If you'd like a quick call to lock this down, I'm available Monday morning PST.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding FinTech's redline and my reply. High level concerns from ops: 90-day backup TTL materially increases snapshot lifecycle cost and retention bookkeeping; for DR we can do 60 days but need to ensure snapshots are not part of any downstream data plane (i.e., no training/analytics).

Proposed operational guardrails (ops_impact_matrix attached):
- Snapshot tombstone on creation (prevents other flows from rehydrating for analytics).
- Single, compressed snapshot manifest delivered monthly showing which customer snapshots passed TTL and were expunged.
- On-demand erasure API for customers to request immediate purge of recoverable copies in scoped regions (we'll require a validation ticket + 48-hour ops window).

Legal considerations: Karthik, Laura — do we need to codify the attestation language for a lawful hold (customer confirmation + case id + expected end date)? We should also define a maximum automatic extension (e.g., single 90-day extension with justification) before requiring an escalated legal review.

Thoughts?

David

Gina — appreciate the flexibility. Summary of agreed points and next steps (for the DPA paragraph):

- Backup snapshot TTL: 60 days. Snapshots will be tombstoned on creation and excluded from training/analytics flows.
- Deletion proof: monthly deletion manifest delivered within 7 business days of month close; manifest will include snapshot ID, creation timestamp, deletion confirmation (manifest entry).
- On-demand erasure API: Redwood will acknowledge requests within 24 hours and complete purges within 72 hours, except where a lawful hold is declared. Requests must include the standard validation ticket and region scope.
- Lawful/investigation holds: Customer may request an initial 90-day hold with attestation (case id + justification); Redwood may apply a single 90-day extension upon documented need, beyond which Redwood will require formal legal process and escalation. All holds will be logged with an audit trail and visible to the customer via the Console.

Operational/implementation notes: Karthik and Laura have reviewed the language and will insert precise attestation phrasing. Ops will implement the monthly manifest export and the on-demand API SLA.
